featureRequest:
This is revision 2 of 2 of a larger feature. Build only this revision.

The whole feature, as the person asked for it:
# Projects | Files tabs in the expanded sidebar (and 5 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
The Files explorer sits at the bottom of the one scrolling sidebar, after every app and its terminals. The more apps someone has, the further down they must scroll to find it, and it never shows when the sidebar is collapsed to the rail. The developer wants two tabs at the top of the sidebar: Projects (Home plus the apps and terminals) and Files (the explorer). The rail gets a Projects icon and a Files icon that expand the pane onto that tab. Two small additions keep users from losing context once the lists are on separate tabs: the Files header names the app it is showing, and the Projects tab label shows a rollup status dot.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Projects | Files tabs in the expanded sidebar (confirmed)
Add a two-tab strip at the top of the expanded sidebar, below or beside the existing collapse button («). The Projects tab holds what the sidebar shows today: the Home row and each app with its terminals. The Files tab holds only the explorer (the `explorer` ReactNode prop), filling the sidebar height, so nobody has to scroll past the apps to reach it. Today the explorer is rendered after the apps at Sidebar.tsx:114 inside the single scrolling nav (.sidebar overflow-y: auto, Sidebar.module.css:1-8; .explorerSlot at Sidebar.module.css:131-136). Only the active tab's content is shown. Make the tabs accessible (role=tablist/tab/tabpanel, aria-selected). Picking an app, a terminal, Home or a file must never switch tabs by itself; the tab only changes when the user picks one (tab click, rail icon, or shortcut). Not included: a split view or a draggable divider.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.tsx:79-114 (apps rendered first, explorer last at line 114)
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.module.css:1-8 (.sidebar overflow-y: auto)
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.module.css:131-136 (.explorerSlot)

### 2. Rail gets Projects and Files icons (confirmed)
In the collapsed rail (Sidebar.tsx:40-64), keep Expand (»), Home and the app initials with their status dots, and add two icons: Projects and Files. Clicking either one expands the pane (same effect as onTogglePane / Ctrl+B) and shows that tab. Show which tab is active in the rail, for example with the existing railOn style. Give both icons aria-labels and titles. Update the prop comment at Sidebar.tsx:19 ('never in the rail'), which stops being true. Sidebar.explorer.test.tsx:52 covers the explorer in the collapsed rail and must be updated to the new behaviour.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.tsx:40-64 (rail has only Expand, Home, app initials)
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.tsx:19 (comment: explorer never in the rail)
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.explorer.test.tsx:52
- Developer: 'rail gets Projects and Files icons; clicking one expands to that tab'

### 3. Files header names whose files are shown (confirmed)
The explorer root follows context (root.ts:68-87): the selected app, the app that owns the active editor tab, a Misc file's folder, or Home. The panel header shows only the folder name (ExplorerPanel.tsx:295-297). Once the apps are on another tab, users can't see which app the files belong to. Make the Files header show the app's name, or 'Misc' or 'Home', as well as the folder name. Do not change how the root is chosen; root.ts logic stays as it is.

Evidence:
- src/features/explorer/root.ts:68-87
- src/features/explorer/ExplorerPanel.tsx:295-297

### 4. Rollup status dot on the Projects tab label (confirmed)
While Files is open, the app and terminal status dots are hidden. Show one StatusDot on the Projects tab label (and its rail icon, if that fits) that rolls up all apps. Reuse the existing helpers: rollup() in src/state/model.ts:135-142 (red if any failed, green if all up, amber if some up or stopping, grey otherwise) applied to the executable terminals of all apps, the same filter the per-app dot uses (Sidebar.tsx:38, `app.terminals.filter(isExecutable)`). The tab label must still read clearly with the dot. This was proposed by the assistant and accepted as part of the build, but it hasn't been tried with users yet.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.tsx:38 (appRollup using rollup + isExecutable)
- src/features/apps/Sidebar.tsx:95 (per-app StatusDot)
- src/state/model.ts:135-142 (rollup)

### 5. Remember the last tab across restarts (confirmed)
Save the active tab in localStorage next to the collapsed state, which uses the key 'td.sidebarCollapsed' (App.tsx:64-71 COLLAPSE_KEY/readCollapsed, App.tsx:94 useState). Use a new key in the same style, e.g. 'td.sidebarTab' with 'projects' or 'files', default 'projects', and read it in a try/catch like readCollapsed. Existing tests say td.sidebarCollapsed is the only key saved (App.test.tsx:499, App.layout.test.tsx:349). Update them to allow the new key; do not drop the check.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:64-71
- src/App.tsx:94
- src/App.test.tsx:499
- src/App.layout.test.tsx:349

### 6. Ctrl+Shift+E opens the Files tab (confirmed)
Add a keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+Shift+E, that shows the Files tab, expanding the pane first if it is collapsed. App shortcuts live in one shared list, src/shared/shortcuts.ts: add an id (e.g. 'showFiles') to AppShortcutId, an entry to APP_SHORTCUTS (label like 'Show Files', keys 'Ctrl+Shift+E'), and a case in matchShortcut (ctrl && shift && !alt && key 'e'). Because TerminalHost.tsx:77 passes any isAppShortcut key to the window, a focused terminal will then give the key to the app instead of the shell. That is intended, and it matches how Ctrl+Shift+P works. Handle the new id where App handles the other shortcut ids. Ctrl+Shift+E is not used today: matchShortcut only matches Ctrl+B, F5, Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+Alt+T. The palette and help list may show the new entry automatically from APP_SHORTCUTS. Check src/shared/shortcuts.test.ts, which may need a new case.

Evidence:
- src/shared/shortcuts.ts:1 (AppShortcutId)
- src/shared/shortcuts.ts:11-16 (APP_SHORTCUTS)
- src/shared/shortcuts.ts:36-43 (matchShortcut)
- src/features/terminals/TerminalHost.tsx:77 (isAppShortcut bubbles to window)

## Not part of this
- A split layout (projects on top, Files below) with a draggable or resizable divider: discussed and rejected in favour of tabs.
- Any change to how the explorer picks its root folder (src/features/explorer/root.ts stays as it is).
- Switching tabs automatically when an app, terminal or file is selected: explicitly not wanted.

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Whether the rollup dot on the Projects tab is useful in practice has not been tried with users; build it as described.
- Exact icon glyphs for the Projects and Files rail buttons and exact tab styling were not specified; follow the existing rail and sidebar styles.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: The left sidebar has two tabs: Projects, which shows the existing apps and their terminals, and Files, which shows the file system explorer.
  - Done when: Selecting the Projects tab shows the apps and terminals list and no file explorer.
  - Done when: Selecting the Files tab shows the file system explorer and not the apps and terminals list.
- **R2**: The Files tab can be reached without scrolling vertically through the project list, no matter how many apps or terminals are listed.
  - Done when: With enough apps and terminals to overflow the sidebar, the Files tab is still visible and selectable without scrolling in the sidebar.
- **R3**: The collapsed sidebar rail shows a Projects icon and a Files icon alongside Expand, Home and the app initials; clicking the Projects icon expands the sidebar and opens the Projects tab, and clicking the Files icon expands the sidebar and opens the Files tab.
  - Done when: From the collapsed rail, clicking the Projects icon expands the sidebar and shows the Projects tab.
  - Done when: From the collapsed rail, clicking the Files icon expands the sidebar and shows the Files tab.
  - Done when: The collapsed rail still shows Expand, Home and the app initials as well as the two new icons.

Not part of this: Changing which root folder the file system explorer shows; Adding, renaming, moving or deleting files from the sidebar; Redesigning the apps-and-terminals list itself

<!--devteam-requirements:-->

These parts are already built and committed on this branch (use them, do not rebuild them):
- Revision 1: R1 to R5 (commit 3eddd42)

This revision builds exactly these requirements (R6 to R10):
- R6: The Files header shows both the context the explorer is following and the current folder's name: the app's name for an app root, 'Misc' for a loose file's folder, or 'Home' for the user's home folder, together with the folder name it shows today.
- R7: The Projects tab label carries one status dot that rolls up all apps' executable terminals using the existing roll-up rules (red if any failed, green if all up, amber if some up or stopping, grey otherwise), and the rail's Projects icon shows the same dot where the existing rail style allows; the label still reads clearly with the dot.
- R8: The active sidebar tab is remembered across restarts in localStorage under the key 'td.sidebarTab' with the value 'projects' or 'files'; when the key is missing, unreadable or holds any other value, the app starts on Projects, and expanding after a collapse shows the tab that was active before collapsing.
- R9: Pressing Ctrl+Shift+E shows the Files tab, expanding the sidebar first when it is collapsed; the shortcut is added to the single shared app-shortcut list so the command palette and help list it, and a focused terminal hands the combination to the app instead of the shell.
- R10: Switching away from the Files tab and back returns to the folder and expanded levels the user was viewing; a tab switch does not reset the explorer's navigation or scroll.

findings.description: The one status indicator visible while Files is open is hidden from assistive technology, so the roll-up is conveyed to sighted users only; expose it without changing the tab/button names (e.g. reference the dot's label from the tab and rail button with aria-describedby, or render a visually hidden status line), keeping the accessible names exactly "Projects"/"Files" and the existing role=img counts intact.
findings.evidence: The new Projects roll-up StatusDot is wrapped in <span aria-hidden="true"> in the tab label (SidebarTabs.tsx:39-41) and again on the rail Projects button (Sidebar.tsx:110-113). StatusDot itself carries role="img" aria-label/title "App status: <rollup>" (src/features/terminals/StatusDot.tsx:16-18), and for a rollup that label is the only non-colour carrier (the only glyph it renders is the greyTick tick, which rollup() never returns). R7's whole purpose is that this single dot is the only status shown while Files is open, yet because of aria-hidden assistive technology now gets nothing: a screen-reader user on the Files tab cannot be told that a terminal failed, while every existing per-app and per-terminal dot is exposed with a label (SidebarProjects.tsx:73 and :85). That is inconsistent with the app's own accessible-status pattern and with USR-006 section 5.6 (consistency) and 5.8 (assistive technology is a requirement).
findings.note: Assistive technology now receives the Projects roll-up without changing any accessible name or role=img count. The visible StatusDot stays decorative (SidebarTabs.tsx:43-45; Sidebar.tsx:114-116), and the tab is wired to a visually hidden line via aria-describedby in the mount effect (SidebarTabs.tsx:73) whose span carries 'App status: {projectsRollup}' (SidebarTabs.tsx:103-105); the rail Projects button gets the same treatment with aria-describedby={railProjectsStatusId} (Sidebar.tsx:111) and its own hidden span (Sidebar.tsx:118-120). Sidebar.tabs.test.tsx 'REV-1 R7' tests assert toHaveAccessibleName('Projects') and toHaveAccessibleDescription('App status: red' / 'App status: grey') on both the tab and the rail button, and that getAllByRole('img', ...) still returns only the two per-app dots, so the tab/button names and status-image counts are unchanged. Ran npx vitest run on Sidebar.tabs/Sidebar.explorer/Sidebar.collapse (43 passed), ExplorerPanel (47 passed), App.explorer/App.shortcuts/CommandPalette/TerminalHost.shortcuts/shortcuts (98 passed); npm run lint (tsc --noEmit) is clean. The only whole-suite failures are the pre-existing App.test.tsx/App.version.test.tsx 2.3.0-vs-2.4.0 assertions and a pre-existing load-sensitive race in App.explorer.test.tsx's R9 rename test, which passes when that file runs alone.

findings.description: The performance acceptance check for R10's tab switch - 300 apps and 3,000 terminals, panel update under 100 ms - has no test at that size and no timing assertion at all.
findings.evidence: The only tab-switch scale proof is 'R2: switching tabs does not reconcile the 500-row Projects list', built from manyApps(50, 10) = 50 apps / 500 terminals, and it asserts only that stateOf is not re-read. No fixture uses the performance requirement's 300 apps / 3,000 terminals and nothing measures the 100 ms budget (no performance.now/Date.now around the switch), so a switch that took seconds at the stated size would still pass every test.
findings.note: src/features/apps/Sidebar.tabs.test.tsx:267 adds 'R10: with 300 apps and 3,000 terminals, switching Projects -> Files -> Projects updates the panel in under 100 ms without remounting the loaded explorer'. It builds manyApps(300, 10) = 300 apps and 3,000 terminals, warms the Files panel, resolves the tab elements before timing, brackets the two fireEvent clicks with performance.now(), asserts elapsed < 100, and asserts the mounted explorer's listing/mount count stays at 1. I ran npx vitest run on this file (31 passed) and on all seven changed test files (176 passed), and npm run lint (tsc --noEmit) passed; a switch that took seconds at this size or remounted the explorer would now fail the test.

findings.description: The edge case 'truncated without hiding the Up and Show hidden controls' is proven for the DOM controls but not for the layout that actually keeps them visible; a CSS-module assertion like the R2 strip tests would close it.
findings.evidence: The long-name test only asserts the Up and Show hidden buttons are present and that the title attribute holds the full 'context / folder' text. It never asserts the truncation CSS (.context/.folder text-overflow: ellipsis, .action flex: none), so removing the ellipsis or letting the title grow would not fail any test.

findings.description: The 'or stopping' half of the R7 amber rule has no independent test (e.g. all-stopping/stopped with no running terminal).
findings.evidence: The amber case feeds t1=running and t2=stopping, which is already amber from the 'some up' branch, so the 'or stopping' clause is never exercised on its own. A projectsRollup that dropped stopping-only states would still pass this suite.
